domain_characteristics.detection_complexity: moderate to high due to text-heavy, socially engineered content with variable linguistic styles and obfuscation
data_characteristics: presence of obfuscated or suspicious domain names
contains both short and long email bodies

common_indicators: presence of suspicious URLs often unrelated to sender domain
use of urgent or lucrative offers in subject lines (e.g., 'Part-Time opportunity - $2000/week')
inclusion of financial or personal gain narratives (e.g., inheritance scams, fake job offers)
presence of misspellings, grammatical errors, and unusual formatting
inclusion of contact information with free email providers or suspicious domains
references to well-known brands or institutions to build trust (e.g., Barclays Bank, Canadian Pharmacy)
use of obfuscated or non-standard URLs with uncommon TLDs or domain names
inclusion of pharmaceutical product promotions with direct links
use of social engineering tactics appealing to emotions or urgency
attack_signatures: signature pattern 1: Emails containing financial scams referencing large abandoned sums with detailed backstories and requests for cooperation (e.g., 'I am Mr. Tim Kennedy, senior credit officer... abandoned sum of 12.5 million British pounds')
signature pattern 2: Phishing emails promoting online pharmacies with direct URLs and claims of FDA approval or discounts (e.g., 'fast loading us based online pharmacy http://www.nmedbuy.org/')
signature pattern 3: Use of short, spam-like bodies with lists of cheap medications and embedded suspicious URLs (e.g., 'Viagra >>>> High Quality... http://adhviw.summerballs.info/?38872604')
technical_markers: measurable marker 1: URLs with uncommon or newly registered domains, often with numeric or random character strings (e.g., 'http://asterduskyhah.com/')
measurable marker 2: Subject lines containing monetary amounts or urgent calls to action (e.g., '$2000/week', 'Online Drugstore Announce Discounts')
measurable marker 3: Email bodies exceeding 500 words with narrative scams or social engineering content, often including personal names and contact details
attack_vectors: email phishing via deceptive email content
malicious URLs directing to fraudulent or malicious websites
exploit_techniques: use of emotional appeals and urgency to bypass rational scrutiny
embedding of obfuscated or shortened URLs to evade URL-based filters
inclusion of contact information to establish false legitimacy
leveraging common phishing themes such as financial windfalls and health products

typical_behaviors: benign emails with professional or neutral subject lines related to business, academic, or news content
email bodies containing structured, coherent, and topic-consistent text without suspicious links
absence of unsolicited financial offers or urgent calls to action
presence of legitimate organizational signatures and contact information consistent with sender domain
use of standard language and formatting with minimal spelling or grammatical errors
baseline_metrics: average email body length typically between 100 to 1000 words depending on context
URLs, if present, correspond to known or reputable domains matching sender source
subject lines generally descriptive without monetary or urgent inducements
low frequency of suspicious or obfuscated URLs (<5% of benign emails)
absence of repeated suspicious keywords such as 'discount', 'free', 'urgent', or monetary amounts
operational_patterns: legitimate emails often contain references to organizational events, research, or transactional information
benign emails include formal salutations and closings consistent with professional communication
use of recognized domain names and email addresses consistent with the source field
absence of unsolicited attachments or embedded scripts
consistent formatting and language style aligned with sender's organizational context
normal_thresholds: flag emails with >1 suspicious URL or URLs with uncommon TLDs
flag subject lines containing monetary values or urgent phrases
flag emails with body length exceeding 500 words containing narrative financial scams
flag presence of free or public email addresses in contact info within financial context
flag emails with >3 spelling or grammatical errors in business context

industry_context: feature engineering from text and metadata

current_threats: phishing emails exploiting financial scams and online pharmacy promotions
social engineering attacks leveraging emotional and urgent appeals
use of obfuscated URLs to evade detection
impersonation of trusted institutions to gain victim trust
emerging_patterns: increased use of narrative-rich emails with detailed backstories
diversification of phishing themes beyond financial scams to health and employment
use of multi-source data blending to evade single-source detection models
inclusion of legitimate-looking contact details to increase credibility
risk_factors: high variability in email language and style
presence of newly registered or suspicious domains in URLs
lack of sender authentication or mismatched sender metadata
use of free or public email services for contact addresses
long email bodies with complex narratives increasing detection difficulty
threat_landscape.threat_sophistication: moderate sophistication with social engineering and URL obfuscation, but lacking advanced evasion such as polymorphic content or encrypted payloads

detection_rules: flag emails with subject lines containing monetary amounts or urgent offers
flag emails containing URLs with uncommon or suspicious TLDs or domain patterns
flag emails with narrative content describing financial windfalls or inheritance scams
flag emails containing contact information using free or suspicious email domains
flag emails with multiple spelling or grammatical errors in business contexts
monitoring_recommendations: implement URL reputation and domain age checks for embedded links
monitor for repeated use of common phishing keywords and phrases
track sender domain consistency and authentication results (SPF, DKIM, DMARC)
use natural language processing to detect social engineering narrative patterns
correlate email source metadata with content-based risk indicators
threshold_suggestions: alert on presence of >1 suspicious URL per email
alert on subject lines containing '$' or 'discount' keywords
alert on emails with body length >500 words containing financial scam keywords
alert on contact emails from free providers in financial or health-related contexts
alert on emails with >3 spelling/grammar errors in professional communication
pattern_matching: use regex to detect monetary expressions and urgent call-to-action phrases in subject and body
pattern match URLs against known phishing domain blacklists and suspicious TLDs
apply NLP models to identify scam narrative structures and impersonation attempts
detect presence of contact info patterns inconsistent with sender domain
match against known phishing email templates and linguistic markers
